objective: Al terminar hablas de obligaciones y capacidades en el pasado con had to, didn't have to, could, was able to y managed to.

warmup.prompt_es: 'Tuve que trabajar los domingos', 'no pude abrir la puerta', 'conseguí terminarlo'. En el pasado no todos los modales funcionan igual: había que elegir bien.

lines.speaker: Rita
lines.text: How was your first job? Was it hard?

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: Quite hard. I had to get up at five every morning and I couldn't take weekends off.
lines.es: Bastante. Tenía que levantarme a las cinco y no podía librar los fines de semana.

lines.speaker: Rita
lines.text: Did you have to wear a uniform?

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: No, we didn't have to, but we had to look smart. I could use my own phone at work, which was great.
lines.es: No, no teníamos que hacerlo, pero sí presentarnos bien. Podía usar mi propio móvil en el trabajo, lo cual era genial.

lines.speaker: Rita
lines.text: And were you able to learn anything useful?

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: Yes! On the first day I couldn't use the cash machine, but by the end of the week I was able to serve customers alone.
lines.es: ¡Sí! El primer día no sabía usar la caja, pero al final de la semana pude atender a los clientes solo.

lines.speaker: Rita
lines.text: Did you ever have a problem with a customer?
lines.es: ¿Tuviste alguna vez un problema con un cliente?

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: Once. A man was very angry, but I managed to calm him down and he left a big tip.
lines.es: Una vez. Un hombre estaba furioso, pero conseguí calmarlo y dejó una buena propina.

glossary.example: I need to take time off.
I managed to finish on time.
I was able to help him.

md_es: | *must / have to* | ***had to*** | *I **had to** get up at five.* |
| *don't have to* | ***didn't have to*** | *We **didn't have to** wear a uniform.* |
| *Do you have to?* | ***Did you have to?*** | ***Did** you **have to** work Saturdays?* |
(*Must* no tiene pasado: se usa *had to*.)
**Capacidad en pasado: could, was able to, managed to**
| capacidad **general** en el pasado | *could* o *was able to* | *I **could** swim when I was five.* |
| **una vez**, tras un esfuerzo (lo conseguí) | *was able to / managed to* | *I **managed to** calm him down.* · *I **was able to** fix it yesterday.* |
| no pude (general o una vez) | *couldn't / wasn't able to* | *I **couldn't** open the door.* |
**Regla:** en afirmativa, *could* se usa para capacidad **general**; para un éxito **concreto** usa *was able to* o *managed to*. En negativa, *couldn't* sirve para ambos.
**Permisos en pasado:** *We could use our phones* (nos dejaban) · *We weren't allowed to park there.*
**Ojo:** *I could see / hear / smell / understand…* con verbos de percepción y mente se usa could, no was able to: *I could hear music.*

common_mistakes_es.wrong: I could finish it yesterday (con esfuerzo).
common_mistakes_es.right: I managed to finish it yesterday.

key_phrases: I had to … · I didn't have to …
I could … when I was young
I managed to … · I was able to …
